articles.title: Gujarat Launches India's First State-Level Sports Genomics Programme - Drishti IAS
articles.content: National Current Affairs Prev Next Gujarat Launches India’s First State-Level Sports Genomics Programme 02 Sep 2026 2 min read Why in News? Gujarat has launched India’s first State-level Sports Genomics Programme to bring genomics, sports science, physiology and nutrition together for scientific athlete identification, training and high-performance development . Key Points First in India: Gujarat has become the first Indian state to launch a Sports Genomics Programme . Implementing Agency: The programme is being driven by the Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre (GBRC) under the Department of Science and Technology . Scientists have started collecting athlete samples, with the first batch collected from tennis players of the Gujarat State Tennis Association . The next phase will cover athletes in archery, fencing, judo and shooting associated with the Vijayi Bharat Foundation . Annual Target: Gujarat aims to collect around 2,000 athlete samples per year . Around 10,000 athlete samples are proposed to be collected and analysed over five years . Sports Genomics: It studies how genetic variations may be associated with athletic traits such as muscle composition, endurance, metabolism, exercise response, recovery and injury susceptibility. No Single Sports Gene: The programme recognises that sporting success depends on a combination of genetics, training, coaching, nutrition, infrastructure, lifestyle and environmental factors. Whole-Genome Sequencing: The programme proposes whole-genome sequencing of talented athletes to study and validate genetic markers associated with endurance, power and other performance traits . Gujarat Athlete Genome Database: G-AGD is proposed to integrate genetic, physiological and performance data for long-term research and athlete profiling. Age Groups: Athletes below 14 years, 14 to under 18 years and above 18 years are proposed to be covered. Sports Biotechnology Hub: The programme aims to strengthen Gujarat’s position as a Sports Biotechnology Innovation Hub . articles.title: Odisha Lok Bhavan becomes country's first IGBC Platinum-certified green campus
articles.content: Renewable 3 min read Odisha Lok Bhavan becomes country's first IGBC Platinum-certified green campus Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati received the certification from IGBC National Chairman C Sekhar Reddy at a function held at New Abhishek Hall at Lok Bhavan here on Tuesday. PTI Published On Sep 2, 2026 at 12:57 PM IST Select ETEnergyworld as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook The Lok Bhavan campus scored 88 out of 100 points, placing it in the highest category of the IGBC rating system. The Odisha Lok Bhavan here has become the first Governor House in the country to receive the Indian Green Building Council (IGBC) Platinum certification under its Green Campus Rating System, marking a significant step towards sustainable and environment-friendly infrastructure, an official statement said on Tuesday. Governor Hari Babu Kambhampati received the certification from IGBC National Chairman C Sekhar Reddy at a function held at New Abhishek Hall at Lok Bhavan here on Tuesday. The Lok Bhavan campus scored 88 out of 100 points, placing it in the highest category of the IGBC rating system. Advt "Odisha's Lok Bhavan becomes India's first Lok Bhavan to be certified green and Platinum and also the first ever Platinum Rated campus under the revised and stringent IGBC Green Campus v1 rating system (launched July 2024). It is also the First Lok Bhavan in the country to adopt an all-electric official carcade," the Governor's House said in a statement. Speaking to reporters on the occasion, Kambhampati described the recognition as a proud moment for Odisha and said the certification reflected concerted efforts to transform the Lok Bhavan into a green campus. "The certification recognises the green cover, clean energy generation and use of electric vehicles, among other initiatives. Whatever steps were suggested were taken up by Lok Bhavan, and ultimately we achieved the highest rating," the governor said. Kambhampati said he would show the certificate to Prime Minister Narendra Modi during his next visit to Delhi and expressed hope that the achievement would encourage other institutions to adopt sustainable practices and seek green certification. Taking the message beyond Lok Bhavan, the governor urged universities across Odisha to obtain green certification and play a greater role in creating environmental awareness. Thousands of students pass through university campuses every year and could become ambassadors of environmental protection, he said. The governor also highlighted the renewable energy measures taken at Lok Bhavan. The campus currently has an installed solar power capacity of 635 kWp, he said, urging households and institutions to make greater use of rooftop solar systems. articles.title: ISRO To Launch EOS-05 On GSLV-F17 On September 4; India Set For New 'Eye In The Sky'
articles.content: Updated 2 September 2026 at 11:17 IST The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is launching EOS-05, India's first geosynchronous imaging satellite, aboard the GSLV-F17 rocket on September 4, 2026, at 2:55 am IST from Sriharikota. Weighing about 2,367 kg, EOS-05 will enable frequent imaging for weather, disaster management, agriculture, and environmental monitoring. Melvin Narayan Science News 3 min read Follow : ISRO To Launch EOS-05 On GSLV-F17 | Image: ISRO New Delhi: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) is set to return to the launch pad with a major Earth-observation mission as it prepares to launch EOS-05 aboard the GSLV-F17 rocket on September 4, 2026. The mission will mark a significant milestone for India's space programme, with EOS-05 becoming the country's first-ever imaging satellite to operate from geosynchronous orbit. The launch is scheduled for 2:55 am IST on September 4 from the Second Launch Pad at the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota, Andhra Pradesh. GSLV-F17 is the 19th flight of India's Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle and will carry EOS-05 into a Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (Sub-GTO). Weighing approximately 2,367 kg, EOS-05 is designed to provide frequent imaging of large regions from a high-altitude orbit. Its geosynchronous positioning will enable it to maintain a persistent view of the Indian subcontinent, offering a major advantage over conventional Earth-observation satellites that revisit locations at longer intervals. What Will EOS-05 Do? EOS-05 is being positioned as a new "eye in the sky" for India, with applications spanning weather observation, disaster management, agriculture and environmental monitoring. Advertisement The satellite's imaging capabilities are expected to help monitor cyclones, floods, forest fires and other rapidly developing natural disasters, while also supporting agricultural assessment and natural-resource mapping. Its ability to repeatedly image a broad geographical area could provide more timely information for authorities during emergencies. The mission is particularly significant because geosynchronous imaging can offer much more frequent observations of a region than traditional Earth-observation satellites in lower orbits. This could strengthen India's ability to track fast-changing weather systems and other events in near real time. Advertisement GSLV-F17: 19th GSLV Flight The EOS-05 spacecraft will be launched using GSLV-F17, the 19th flight of India's Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle. The rocket is equipped with an indigenous cryogenic upper stage and features a four-metre-diameter ogive composite payload fairing for the mission. GSLV-F17 will initially inject EOS-05 into a Sub-GTO. The spacecraft will then use its onboard propulsion system to raise itself towards its intended geosynchronous orbit. Mission Comes Five Years After EOS-03 Setback The upcoming launch also carries significance because EOS-05 is the successor to EOS-03, also known as GISAT-1, which was lost during the GSLV-F10 mission in August 2021. The earlier mission failed after an anomaly in the rocket's cryogenic upper stage, preventing EOS-03 from reaching orbit. ISRO's current GSLV-F17 mission therefore represents a renewed attempt to establish India's geosynchronous Earth-imaging capability. If successful, EOS-05 will give India a new capability to conduct frequent, wide-area Earth observation from geosynchronous orbit, potentially strengthening applications ranging from weather forecasting and disaster...

articles.title: StarManch Introduces a First-of-Its-Kind In-Car Karaoke Experience - Ahmedabad Mirror
articles.content: Indian homegrown karaoke platform founded by Randeep Bhattacharya takes its 8,000+ song catalogue beyond smartphones and into connected mobility Kolkata (West Bengal) [India], September 1: StarManch, an Indian homegrown karaoke and social music platform, has entered the connected-mobility space through its integration with the newly launched MG Hector Tomahawk. The development takes StarManch beyond smartphones and introduces a first-of-its-kind interactive karaoke experience within the vehicle’s entertainment ecosystem. Through the StarManch Karaoke app, occupants can select songs, sing along and record their performances inside the car. Backed by a catalogue of more than 8,000 karaoke tracks across Bollywood, regional, devotional and children’s music, the platform transforms the vehicle cabin into an interactive entertainment space for families, friends and music enthusiasts. The MG Hector Tomahawk features what the automaker describes as India’s first Gen AI-powered in-car karaoke experience. Unlike conventional in-car entertainment, which primarily focuses on listening to streamed music, the StarManch experience encourages occupants to actively participate, perform and create shared musical memories. The integration represents a significant expansion for StarManch, founded by Bengali entrepreneur and music enthusiast Randeep Bhattacharya. Conceived as a platform to make singing accessible and social, StarManch has now evolved from a mobile karaoke application into an entertainment technology offering for connected vehicles. Whether it is families singing together during a weekend trip, friends revisiting popular classics on a road journey or aspiring singers building confidence through music, StarManch aims to make travel more engaging and participative. The development also highlights the growing contribution of Indian technology brands to the connected-mobility ecosystem. As vehicles increasingly evolve into digitally enabled lifestyle spaces, interactive features such as karaoke are expanding the role of in-car entertainment beyond conventional audio and video streaming. Speaking about the development, Randeep Bhattacharya, Founder of StarManch, said, “Kolkata has always been a city where music is woven into everyday life. Growing up here inspired my love for music and storytelling. Our vision with StarManch has always been to make singing more accessible and social. Taking karaoke beyond smartphones and into people’s everyday journeys is an important step in that direction. We do not want people to simply listen to music—we want them to become part of it.” For StarManch, the integration opens a new growth avenue beyond mobile devices and demonstrates how an Indian homegrown entertainment platform can become part of mainstream automotive experiences. It also reflects changing consumer expectations, with connected vehicles increasingly being viewed as interactive spaces for entertainment, communication and shared experiences. articles.title: IIT Madras launches digital systems audit certification on SWAYAM Plus
articles.content: News Facebook Twitter WhatsApp Linkedin Copy URL The Indian Institute of Technology Madras (IIT Madras), in collaboration with the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG), has introduced a new online Certification on Audit of Digital Systems (CADS) through the SWAYAM Plus platform. The four-month programme is designed to build specialised skills for auditing increasingly complex digital systems used by governments and enterprises. The foundation-level certification focuses on emerging areas such as Artificial Intelligence, cybersecurity, digital public infrastructure, cloud technologies, information systems and data-driven services. The programme aims to prepare professionals to assess technology-enabled systems and identify risks associated with digital operations. Developed jointly by experts from CAG, IIT Madras and IITM Pravartak, the curriculum combines online learning with practical case studies, self-assessment exercises and real-world audit scenarios. Learners will also undergo proctored computer-based assessments as part of the certification process. Also Read: Prof. T. G. Sitharam appointed as Advisor of IIT Kharagpur The programme is aligned with the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 and National Credit Framework (NCrF), providing recognised academic credit alongside professional training. The broader CADS programme includes six foundational domains, with each course carrying 45 hours of learning. articles.title: Odisha Lok Bhavan Gets India's First IGBC Platinum Green Campus Tag - KalingaTV
articles.content: Odisha Lok Bhavan Gets India’s First IGBC Platinum Green Campus Tag Odisha Lok Bhavan becomes India’s first IGBC Platinum Green Campus, scoring 88 points for its work in solar energy, water conservation, biodiversity and sustainability. By Vinay Kakkad On Sep 2, 2026 Share Advertisement Bhubaneswar: Odisha’s Lok Bhavan has secured the Platinum rating under the Indian Green Building Council’s (IGBC) Green Campus Rating System, becoming the first Lok Bhavan in India to receive the distinction. The campus scored 88 out of 100 points, placing it in the highest IGBC certification category. It is also the first campus to achieve a Platinum rating under the revised IGBC Green Campus Version 1, introduced in July 2024. The certification was formally presented to Odisha Governor Dr Hari Babu Kambhampati by IGBC National Chairman C. Shekar Reddy at a programme held at the New Abhishek Hall at Lok Bhavan on Tuesday. The recognition follows a wide-ranging assessment of the government campus covering energy use, water conservation, biodiversity, waste management, sustainable transport, site planning, health and well-being, and day-to-day operations. Campus records strong green credentials More than 80% of Lok Bhavan’s campus remains under green cover. A biodiversity assessment identified 2,374 trees belonging to 72 species, while 27 faunal species were also recorded. The campus has a Shannon-Wiener diversity index of 3.59. The grounds also include a deer park and Atal Van, an ecological park dedicated to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee. The park features a T-55 battle tank and a Rafale model among its collection of defence and naval artefacts. Reflective roofing and the extensive vegetation have also contributed to efforts to reduce the heat-island effect around the campus. Energy management formed another major part of the certification. Lok Bhavan has an installed 635 kWp solar photovoltaic system, while major electricity-consuming systems are monitored and metered. Its Energy Performance Index is 50.57 kWh per square metre per year, putting the campus on a path towards net-zero operations. The current solar capacity followed the commissioning of a 485 kWp rooftop solar plant in June 2026. The installation spans several buildings, including the Abhishek Banquet Hall, Campus Garage, Administrative Building, Governor’s House, Energy Park, Police ADC Residence, Naval ADC Residence and Wellness Centre. The project was executed by NBCC (India) Limited. Water use falls by more than 35% Water conservation has also produced measurable results at the campus. Lok Bhavan has recorded a more than 35% reduction in water consumption, supported by water-efficient fixtures and a broader rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge network. Advertisement The system includes recharge trenches, filter chambers, ponds and borewell recharge structures. Irrigation has also been redesigned through drip irrigation and controlled sprinklers, while separate monitoring is maintained for municipal water supply, building operations, kitchen use and irrigation. Waste management practices were assessed as part of the certification as well. Waste is segregated at source, while organic material generated by kitchens and landscaping is processed through vermicomposting. The final assessment recorded 100% treatment and reuse of the reported organic waste and...

articles.title: ISRO chairman Narayanan visits Tirumala; presents models of GSLV-F17, EOS-05 satellite to deity
articles.content: Tirumala: ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan visited the Tirumala temple on Wednesday and offered prayers to Lord Venkateswara along with his team during the VIP break darshan. Narayanan reached Ananda Nilayam through the Vaikuntha Q Complex and placed miniature models of the GSLV-F17 launch vehicle and EOS-05 satellite at the feet of the deity as part of the traditional prayers. The models symbolically represented the upcoming mission and were presented at the sanctum sanctorum, seeking the Lord's blessings for its successful launch. The GSLV-F17 model is a miniature representation of ISRO's Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle, a three-stage heavy-lift rocket designed to place satellites into geostationary transfer orbit. The mission's EOS-05 satellite model represents the Earth observation spacecraft that the rocket is scheduled to carry. Following the darshan, temple priests blessed Narayanan and the ISRO team at the Ranganayakula Mandapam and presented them with theertha prasadam and Lord Venkateswara's offerings. The GSLV-F17 mission is scheduled to lift off from the Second Launch Pad of the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR), Sriharikota, at 2.55 a.m. on September 4. Nearly five years after the August 21, 2021 unsuccessful GISAT-1 mission by GSLV-F10 due to a glitch in the cryogenic third upper stage, ISRO will launch the EOS-05 spacecraft, also known as GISAT-1A. It will be India's first-ever imaging satellite to operate from the Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO), using the heavy lift launch vehicle GSLV-MkII. According to ISRO, the three-stage, 51.7 m tall GSLV-F17, with a lift-off mass of 420.5 tonnes, will place the EOS-05 satellite into a Sub-GTO. After liftoff, the 2,367 kg spacecraft will be injected into the Sub-GTO with a perigee of 170 km and an apogee of 28,934 km, with an inclination of about 19.28 Deg (with plus or minus one) to the equator. EOS-05 is a state-of-the-art Earth observation spacecraft. It is India's first-ever imaging satellite from Geosynchronous orbit. EOS-05 is designed to capture detailed images of the Earth and provide data for monitoring and other applications that require regular observation of the land and environment. It aims to improve the existing remote sensing capabilities, and GISATs are designed to image in multi-spectral and hyper-spectral bands to provide near real-time pictures of large areas of the country, under cloud-free conditions, at frequent intervals, which is, a selected field image every 5 minutes and an entire Indian landmass image every 30 minutes at 42 metres (138 ft) spatial resolution.

articles.title: KSEB plans to open 200 fast EV charging stations within a year - The New Indian Express
articles.content: KOCHI: As part of an ambitious plan to boost its electric-vehicle infrastructure, KSEB proposes to open a network of over 200 fast-charging stations across the state within a year and transform the 622km-long stretch of NH 66 into India’s first electric truck corridor over the next four years. Unveiling a study prepared by the Kerala State Electricity Board Ltd (KSEBL), in partnership with The International Council on Clean Transportation (ICCT), at the India Clean Transportation Summit in New Delhi on Tuesday, KSEB director (generation) M P Rajan said Keralam will need Rs 19 crore and 12.5 MW charging capacity to transform NH 66 into India’s first electric truck corridor by 2030. “By building India’s first state-led electric truck corridor along NH 66, Keralam is showing how a state utility can move ahead of the curve to make freight electrification practical and grid-ready,” Rajan said. “It is a fact that electric trucks have not become popular in the country, but studies show that more cargo movers will shift to e-trucks in future,” he told TNIE. “The KSEB has also invited a tender for the installation of 207 fast-charging stations around the state. The process will be finalised within two months. By delivering a full charge in just 20 minutes, these stations will prove handy for electric cars. We plan to provide amenities such as coffee shops and children’s play areas around the stations,” Rajan added. The Union government has allocated Rs 2,000 crore under the PM E-Drive scheme to establish around 72,000 EV charging stations nationwide. articles.content: English News Tech science ISRO EOS 05 Satellite Launch | Geosynchronous Orbit Updates | India News ISRO to launch EOS-05 imaging satellite: How India's 'Eye in the Sky' will monitor and alert natural disasters 12 hours ago Author: Samira Siddiqui Copy link India is preparing to launch a new kind of Earth-observation satellite. ISRO’s GSLV-F17 rocket will carry EOS-05 into a high orbit, allowing the satellite to repeatedly watch large parts of the country from space. The mission is significant not just because of the satellite, but also because it comes after a seven-month gap following the failure of the PSLV-C62 mission in January 2026. If successful, EOS-05 could help India get faster updates during cyclones, floods, forest fires, and other events that can change quickly. Here is everything you need to know about the GSLV-F17 mission and why EOS-05 matters. What is ISRO’s GSLV-F17 mission? GSLV-F17 is ISRO’s upcoming mission to launch EOS-05, an advanced Earth-observation satellite. The rocket will use the GSLV Mk II configuration and place EOS-05 into a Sub-Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit, or Sub-GTO. From there, the satellite will move towards its planned geosynchronous orbit. GSLV-F17 will be the 19th flight of India’s Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle. The rocket is about 51.7 metres tall and weighs around 420.5 tonnes at liftoff. The mission will take off using the four-metre-wide composite ogive payload fairing, which protects the satellite during its journey through the atmosphere. What is EOS-05? EOS-05 is an advanced Earth-observation satellite being developed by ISRO. It is designed to take images of the Earth's surface and provide information that can be used to monitor large areas of land. What makes EOS-05 particularly important is its planned orbit. It will become India’s first imaging satellite to operate from a geosynchronous orbit. At an altitude of nearly 36,000 kilometres, the satellite will have a much wider view of the Earth than satellites flying in low Earth orbit. How is EOS-05 different from other Earth-observation satellites? This image is created using AI and is only for representational purposes. Most Earth-observation satellites are placed in low Earth orbit, where they move around the planet and pass over a particular area at intervals. EOS-05 is different because it is designed to operate from a geosynchronous orbit, much farther from Earth. This gives the satellite a much wider view and allows it to observe the same broad region repeatedly. So, instead of focusing mainly on getting very detailed images of smaller areas, EOS-05 is designed to provide frequent observations over a large area. The biggest advantage is repeat coverage. A satellite in geosynchronous orbit can stay aligned with the same broad region of Earth as the planet rotates. articles.title: DashLoc Launches DashDesk, an AI -Powered Customer Support Platform
articles.content: AI DashLoc Launches DashDesk, an AI-Powered Customer Support Platform ITN · September 1, 2026 · 3 min read Quick Summary New AI-powered helpdesk platform brings omnichannel customer conversations, automation and support operations into a unified workspace DashDesk enables businesses to streamline ticket management, improve response times and enhance customer experiences at scale Launch strengthens DashLoc’s integrated AI-powered MarTech ecosystem across… New AI-powered helpdesk platform brings omnichannel customer conversations, automation and support operations into a unified workspace DashDesk enables businesses to streamline ticket management, improve response times and enhance customer experiences at scale Launch strengthens DashLoc’s integrated AI-powered MarTech ecosystem across discovery, reputation, engagement and customer support Bengaluru, 01st September 2026: DashLoc, an AI-powered MarTech platform helping businesses strengthen their digital presence, customer engagement and online reputation, today announced the launch of DashDesk , an AI-powered customer support platform designed to help businesses manage customer conversations, automate support operations and deliver faster, more consistent experiences from a single workspace. As businesses engage with customers across multiple touchpoints, support teams often have to manage conversations through different platforms and systems. This can make it difficult to maintain context, track requests and ensure timely resolutions. DashDesk brings customer support operations together on a unified platform, enabling businesses to manage tickets, streamline workflows, collaborate across teams and gain greater visibility into customer interactions. Built with AI at its core, DashDesk combines intelligent automation with essential customer support capabilities. The platform enables businesses to manage customer queries through omnichannel ticket management , while features such as AI-assisted ticket routing, workflow automation, SLA management, knowledge base management, customer self-service portals, real-time analytics and CSAT tracking help support teams improve efficiency and consistency. By automating repetitive support processes and intelligently organizing incoming requests, DashDesk allows customer service teams to spend more time addressing complex customer issues. The platform is designed to help businesses reduce manual intervention, improve response and resolution times, and maintain a consistent support experience as customer interactions scale. DashDesk is built to support businesses across customer-centric sectors including retail, healthcare, BFSI, hospitality, automotive, education, telecom, aviation, real estate and e-commerce . Its scalable architecture enables both growing businesses and larger enterprises to manage increasing volumes of customer interactions while maintaining operational visibility. Commenting on the launch, Sumit Singh, Co-Founder & CEO, DashLoc, said: “Customer expectations around support have changed significantly. Businesses today need to respond quickly, maintain context across conversations and provide consistent service across channels. Yet, support operations are often spread across multiple systems, making it difficult for teams to work efficiently. With DashDesk, we are bringing these interactions into one intelligent workspace where AI and automation can take care of repetitive processes while teams focus on meaningful customer conversations. Our aim is to make customer support more connected, efficient and scalable for businesses as they grow.” The launch of DashDesk marks another step in DashLoc’s vision of building an integrated AI-powered platform covering different stages of the customer journey. articles.title: Odisha's Lok Bhavan becomes India's first Platinum certified green Lok Bhavan | Dailyhunt
articles.content: I n the heart of Bhubaneswar, the institution that has housed the Governor of Odisha since 1960 has earned a distinction no comparable campus in India holds. Advertisement Lok Bhavan, renamed from Raj Bhavan in December 2025, is now the country's first Lok Bhavan to receive IGBC Platinum green certification, and the first campus anywhere in India to reach Platinum under the stricter Green Campus v1 rating system introduced in July 2024. The final score was 88 out of 100, inside the Platinum band of 80 to 100 and among the highest rated green campuses in the country. Retrofitting a working campus The harder part is what it took to get there. Green certifications are easier to win on new construction, where efficiency can be designed in before the foundation is poured. Lok Bhavan is a functioning government campus with decades of built infrastructure, daily operations and public engagement running through it. Under Governor Dr. Hari Babu Kambhampati, the campus was assessed system by system. Civil works were carried out, electrical systems upgraded, water management strengthened, energy monitoring introduced, landscaping and irrigation reworked, and waste handling reorganised. Officials, engineers, consultants and stakeholders worked through a roadmap covering eight environmental and operational categories, with every credit evidenced. The category breakdown: site planning and management 23/25, sustainable transportation 7/7, water conservation 13/18, energy efficiency 17/18, material and resource management 8/8, health and well being 6/7, sustainable operation and maintenance 7/8, and innovation in design 7/9. Green cover, solar and water More than 80% of the campus remains under green cover. A biodiversity survey documented 2,374 trees across 72 species, with faunal records spanning 27 species and a Shannon Wiener diversity index of 3.59. A deer park sits within the grounds, alongside Atal Van, the ecological park dedicated to former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee, where a T-55 battle tank and a Rafale model anchor a collection of defence and naval artefacts. On energy, the campus has installed 635 kWp of solar photovoltaic capacity, with major consuming systems metered and tracked. The Energy Performance Index stands at 50.57 kWh per square metre per year, positioning the campus as a candidate for net zero. Water saw the sharpest operational gain: more than 35% reduction in consumption. That came from an integrated rainwater harvesting and groundwater recharge system built around recharge trenches, filter chambers, ponds and borewell recharge structures, combined with drip irrigation, controlled sprinklers, and separate monitoring of municipal supply, building systems, kitchen and irrigation lines. Waste is segregated at source. Organic waste from kitchens and landscaping is treated on site through vermicomposting, with 100% treatment and reuse, while the final review recorded 100% diversion of reported dry waste from landfill. The all electric carcade Lok Bhavan has also become the first in the country to adopt an all electric official carcade, backed by EV charging infrastructure and electric vehicles for internal movement.
